items.title: Understanding the differences between PgBouncer and Amazon RDS Proxy for PostgreSQL connection pooling
items.summary: Compare Amazon RDS Proxy and PgBouncer for PostgreSQL connection pooling on AWS. This post explains how each pooler handles pooling modes, authentication, failover, and session-state pinning, and gives you a framework to choose between a fully managed service and a self-managed pooler.
items.creator: Stephen Wood

items.title: Migrate CLR code to AWS Lambda when upgrading Amazon RDS for SQL Server to 2025
items.summary: After upgrading Amazon RDS for SQL Server to 2017 or later, CLR strict security leaves user-defined CLR assemblies unusable. This post shows how to migrate CLR logic with no native T-SQL equivalent to an AWS Lambda function, invoked from SQL Server 2025 through sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint behind Amazon API Gateway.
items.creator: Raunak Gupta

items.title: Automated blocking and query alerts for Amazon RDS for SQL Server
items.summary: Learn how to build automated email alerts for blocking chains and long-running queries on Amazon RDS for SQL Server. This serverless solution uses AWS Lambda, Amazon CloudWatch, and Amazon SES to detect blocking, identify the root blocker, and send HTML email alerts for approximately $2.57 per month.
items.creator: Sreedhar Reddy Bakkireddy
